session.evaluation_method: Automated analysis of the NEON product API record (https://data.neonscience.org/api/v0/products/DP1.10022.001). The landing-page schema.org JSON-LD is JavaScript-rendered and was not retrievable, so ratings rely on the API metadata; a few items that would be confirmed by the JSON-LD (e.g., explicit encodingFormat, variableMeasured counts) are rated conservatively.

dataset.title: Ground beetles sampled from pitfall traps
dataset.citation: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network). Ground beetles sampled from pitfall traps (DP1.10022.001), RELEASE-2026. https://doi.org/10.48443/q9ne-6b77. Dataset accessed from https://data.neonscience.org on 2026-07-26.

evaluator.name: Automated FAIR4AI Evaluation
evaluator.evaluation_purpose: pilot of the v20260726 checklist + RATING_RUBRIC.md (open-ended use)
evaluator.evaluation_description: Pilot run validating the 96-item FAIR4AI-Bio checklist, the rating rubric, and the reproducible fair4ai-scoring tool. Metadata drawn from the NEON product API; landing-page JSON-LD was not retrievable.

responses.question: Is the funder of the dataset described?
responses.evidence: No funder or funding organization is stated in the product API metadata. NEON is NSF-funded but this is not recorded in the record.
responses.recommendation: Add funder information (e.g., NSF) using DataCite fundingReferences/funderName or schema.org funder so credit and funding provenance are machine-readable.

responses.question: Is a funding ID / grant number provided?
responses.evidence: No award or grant numbers appear in the metadata.
responses.recommendation: Add the NSF cooperative agreement / award numbers via DataCite fundingReferences/awardNumber.

responses.question: Are non-author contributors acknowledged?
responses.evidence: The abstract and SOPs credit parataxonomists and external expert taxonomists (Carnegie Museum of Natural History; Essig Museum, UC Berkeley), but only at the role/organization level.
responses.notes: Contributions described by role, not attributed to named individuals.
responses.recommendation: Name individual contributors (or provide ORCIDs) for the parataxonomist and expert-taxonomist steps to make attribution explicit.

responses.question: Is the purpose of the dataset described?
responses.evidence: productAbstract states the data provide quality-controlled ground-beetle abundance and diversity for biodiversity monitoring at NEON terrestrial sites.

responses.question: Are the data machine-ready (structural fields sufficient to ingest into a pipeline)?
responses.evidence: Data are delivered as structured relational tables via the NEON REST API with documented table relationships (bet_fielddata and child tables), enabling programmatic ingestion.

responses.question: Is there a list of ML/analysis tasks the dataset is engineered to support?
responses.evidence: No list of intended ML tasks is provided; the product is described for ecological monitoring, not for a specific ML task.
responses.recommendation: Add a short list of supported tasks (e.g., species-occurrence modeling, richness estimation) so downstream ML users can judge task-readiness.

responses.question: Can the dataset's origin be traced via persistent identifiers (is it traceable)?
responses.evidence: Each annual RELEASE carries a DOI (e.g., RELEASE-2026 doi:10.48443/q9ne-6b77); biorepository specimens link out via DarwinCore archives; change logs document processing history.

responses.question: Is the language of the (text) data documented?
responses.evidence: The product is tabular occurrence/specimen data with no free-text/NLP corpus; the item is scoped to Text/NLP data.

responses.question: Is a short human-readable summary provided?
responses.evidence: productDescription gives a concise summary ('Taxonomically identified ground beetles and the plots and times from which they were collected').

responses.question: Are keywords/tags provided?
responses.evidence: 22 keywords are provided (e.g., Carabidae, ground beetles, pitfall traps, biodiversity, invasive species, DNA barcoding).

responses.question: Is a data dictionary / codebook provided?
responses.evidence: Variables are described in the NEON beetle User Guide and per-table descriptions, but a single machine-readable data dictionary is not linked directly from the structured product metadata.
responses.recommendation: Publish a machine-readable data dictionary (CSV/JSON) linked from the product record with field names, types, units, and allowed values for every variable.

responses.question: Is a homepage / landing page provided?
responses.evidence: The product has a persistent landing page: https://data.neonscience.org/data-products/DP1.10022.001.

responses.question: Is a curation/processing repository referenced?
responses.evidence: The NEON data portal serves as the curation and distribution repository, with documented processing pipelines referenced in the change logs.

responses.question: Is example code (load/access/transform) provided or linked?
responses.evidence: No example or load code is referenced in the product metadata (NEON's neonUtilities tooling exists but is not linked from this record).
responses.recommendation: Link example access code (e.g., a neonUtilities snippet or notebook) from the product metadata to lower the barrier to programmatic reuse.

responses.question: Is a canonical descriptor paper referenced?
responses.evidence: No peer-reviewed dataset-descriptor publication is referenced; only NEON protocol and science-design documents are linked.
responses.recommendation: Link a peer-reviewed data-descriptor DOI if/when one exists.

responses.question: Is the constituent data source / original data described?
responses.evidence: The source is clearly described as primary field collection via pitfall trapping at NEON terrestrial sites, with lab sorting and taxonomic identification.

responses.question: Are related datasets referenced?
responses.evidence: Fifteen biorepository specimen collections are linked (e.g., CARC-AP, EMEC, INV) with DarwinCore archive access.

responses.question: Are related/citing papers referenced?
responses.evidence: No 'cited by' publications are referenced in the metadata.
responses.recommendation: Add a machine-readable 'cited by' list (DataCite relatedIdentifier[IsCitedBy]) as literature accumulates.

responses.question: Are creators identified?
responses.evidence: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network) is identified as the organizational creator; no individual creators are named.
responses.recommendation: Add individual creators/collectors with ORCIDs alongside the organizational creator.

responses.question: Is a human-readable title provided?
responses.evidence: productName: 'Ground beetles sampled from pitfall traps'.

responses.question: Is a summary/abstract provided?
responses.evidence: A comprehensive productAbstract describes sampling, sorting, identification, archiving, and the expert-taxonomist uncertainty subset.

responses.question: Is the collection/observation date (or range) provided?
responses.evidence: Temporal coverage spans 2013-07 to the present (2026), with collection dates recorded per sampling bout in bet_fielddata.

responses.question: Is the publisher identified?
responses.evidence: NEON is the publisher; data are served from https://data.neonscience.org.

responses.question: Are the file format(s) documented?
responses.evidence: Data are delivered as tabular files (NEON convention is CSV) and JSON via API, but explicit file-format declarations are not present in the retrieved product metadata.
responses.notes: NEON standard is CSV, but the format is not explicitly declared in the record reviewed.
responses.recommendation: Declare file formats explicitly (e.g., text/csv, application/json) via schema.org encodingFormat or DataCite formats.

responses.question: Is the dataset structure / layout described?
responses.evidence: The record documents multiple related tables (bet_fielddata, bet_sorting, bet_parataxonomistID, bet_expertTaxonomistID, bet_archivepooling, bet_identificationHistory) and their roles.

responses.question: Are the individual data instances / files described?
responses.evidence: Each table is described with its content and expected latency (e.g., bet_fielddata 75 days; expert IDs 600 days).

responses.question: Is the organization of records/files and their relationships described?
responses.evidence: productRemarks documents the record model: one record per trapID/plotID/collectDate in bet_fielddata, with zero-to-many child records across sorting, pinning, and expert tables.

responses.question: Are features/attributes documented?
responses.evidence: Fields for counts, taxonomic identities, vertebrate bycatch, location, and dates are documented across tables and detailed in the User Guide.

responses.question: Are technical specifications (sizes, record counts) documented?
responses.evidence: Sampling specifications are given (trap counts per site by era, trap volumes), but digital file sizes and record counts are not stated in the metadata.
responses.recommendation: Add file sizes and approximate record counts per table so users can estimate compute/storage before download.

responses.question: Is the collection date or date range documented?
responses.evidence: Collection dates are recorded per bout; temporal coverage 2013-07 to present is documented.

responses.question: Is the type of source data collected documented?
responses.evidence: Source data type is documented: field observations plus physical specimens collected via pitfall traps, followed by lab sorting and identification.

responses.question: Is the specific upstream data source (link/identifier) provided?
responses.evidence: This is a primary dataset; the item is scoped to derived/compiled datasets that link to upstream sources.

responses.question: Is the curation rationale documented?
responses.evidence: The rationale is documented in the abstract and science-design document: standardized long-term monitoring of ground-beetle abundance and diversity.

responses.question: Is it documented whether this is part of a larger collection/series?
responses.evidence: Documented as part of NEON's Terrestrial Observation System (TOS), collected across all NEON terrestrial sites.

responses.question: Is sensor/instrument metadata provided (link)?
responses.evidence: productSensor is empty; collection is by physical pitfall trapping, not sensor/instrument captures (camera trap, drone, bioacoustics, telemetry, remote sensing).
responses.notes: Modality mismatch; trap configuration itself is documented under methods. Flagged as a scope-boundary case for the instrument.

responses.question: Is quantitative spatial/temporal resolution documented?
responses.evidence: Spatial resolution: traps ~20 m from plot center in cardinal directions with per-trap locations. Temporal resolution: biweekly sampling during the growing season (temperatures >4 C).

responses.question: Is data preparation/processing described?
responses.evidence: Preparation is described: sorting, pinning vs. 95% ethanol archiving, taxonomic identification, and manual QA in the processing pipeline.

responses.question: Is data gridding / interpolation documented?
responses.evidence: The product is point/plot occurrence data; the item is scoped to spatial/remote-sensing gridded products.

responses.question: Are units consistent and documented?
responses.evidence: Measured variables use standardized units (e.g., meters, decimal degrees); higher taxonomy is standardized against NEON taxon tables.

responses.question: Has data anonymization been applied/documented?
responses.evidence: No personal or human-subject data are present; the item is scoped to human/sensitive data.
responses.notes: Scope mismatch (no personal data). Sensitive-species obfuscation is assessed separately under Security/Privacy.

responses.question: Is it documented whether missing values/gaps have been filled?
responses.evidence: A 'samplingImpractical' flag (added 2020) distinguishes temporarily missing from permanently unavailable data; from 2020 a record is generated per scheduled trap even when not collected.

responses.question: If gaps exist, is the handling method described?
responses.evidence: Missing data are flagged rather than imputed; the flagging approach is described but there is no explicit gap-filling method statement.
responses.recommendation: State explicitly that gaps are flagged (not imputed) and document all flag values and meanings in a machine-readable form.

responses.question: Is labeling/re-labeling documented?
responses.evidence: Taxonomic labeling is described; relabeling from expert taxonomists is tracked, with prior determinations archived in bet_identificationHistory (added 2024).

responses.question: Is outlier removal/filtering documented?
responses.evidence: Quality control is referenced (ATBD NEON.DOC.005424) and manual QA is described, but specific outlier-detection criteria are not stated.
responses.recommendation: Document the specific thresholds/rules used to flag or remove anomalous records, distinguishing manual review from automated flags.

responses.question: Are train/validation/test splits defined?
responses.evidence: This is primary observational data not organized into ML splits; the item is scoped to supervised-ML train/val/test datasets.
responses.notes: Scope mismatch. Site- or year-based split guidance would help ML reuse and is a candidate future addition (informational, not a penalty).

responses.question: Is dataset completeness / ongoing status documented?
responses.evidence: Documented as an active, provisional, ongoing monitoring product with annual RELEASEs; new data continue to be added.

responses.question: Have required quality checks been completed?
responses.evidence: A quality-controlled product with multi-level QA: field technicians, parataxonomists, and a subset verified by expert taxonomists; QC governed by an ATBD.

responses.question: Do categorical variables use a controlled vocabulary with a reference?
responses.evidence: Taxonomy follows NEON taxon tables (a controlled vocabulary), but direct machine-resolvable URIs to the vocabularies are not provided in the structured metadata.
responses.recommendation: Provide resolvable URIs to the controlled vocabularies used (NEON taxon tables, ITIS/Catalogue of Life) rather than prose references.

responses.question: Has the dataset been peer-reviewed / expert-reviewed?
responses.evidence: A subset of specimens (up to 467 per site per year) is verified by external expert taxonomists to estimate parataxonomist uncertainty; internal QA is applied.

responses.question: Is the timeliness / update cadence documented?
responses.evidence: Per-table data latency is documented (bet_fielddata 75 days; sorting/parataxonomist/archive 330 days; expert IDs 600 days), and the product is updated on an ongoing basis.

responses.question: Are known sources of bias documented?
responses.evidence: Parataxonomist uncertainty is estimated via expert re-identification and sampling-effort changes are logged, but broader geographic/detection biases are not explicitly discussed as bias.
responses.recommendation: Add an explicit bias section covering site-selection (geographic) bias, seasonal/habitat detection bias, and parataxonomist-vs-expert discrepancy rates.

responses.question: Are known reuse risks documented?
responses.evidence: Limitations that imply reuse risks are logged (sampling-effort reductions affecting temporal comparability; species obfuscation), but they are not framed as explicit reuse risks.
responses.recommendation: Frame the documented limitations as concrete reuse risks (e.g., naive temporal comparisons across the 40->30->18 trap changes).

responses.question: Are known limitations documented?
responses.evidence: Limitations are documented via change logs: reduced sampling effort over time (budget), sensitive-species obfuscation, and COVID-19/flooding sampling gaps.

responses.question: Is it documented whether the data are experimental?
responses.evidence: The metadata make clear the data are standardized observational monitoring (no treatments/controls), i.e., not experimental.

responses.question: If experimental, is the design described?
responses.evidence: The data are observational, so an experimental-design description does not apply.

responses.question: Are supported ML tasks listed (controlled vocabulary)?
responses.evidence: No supported ML tasks are listed in the metadata.
responses.recommendation: List in-scope ML tasks (e.g., species classification, occupancy/richness modeling) to signal task-readiness.

responses.question: Are benchmark / leaderboard results provided?
responses.evidence: No model-evaluation or benchmark results are reported for this dataset.
responses.recommendation: If the dataset is used in benchmarks, link the results; otherwise note none exist yet.

responses.question: Are recommended uses provided?
responses.evidence: The purpose (biodiversity monitoring, abundance/diversity assessment) is stated, but specific analytical/ML usage recommendations are not provided in the structured metadata.
responses.recommendation: Add explicit usage guidance (recommended split strategies, confounders to control for, appropriate downstream tasks).

responses.question: Is prior AI/ML usage history documented?
responses.evidence: No record of prior AI/ML use (models trained/benchmarked) is provided.
responses.recommendation: Document any published AI/ML uses (DataCite relatedIdentifier[IsCitedBy]); add a placeholder inviting reports of AI/ML use.

responses.question: Are out-of-scope / discouraged uses documented?
responses.evidence: No explicit guidance on inappropriate or discouraged uses is provided.
responses.recommendation: Document uses to avoid (e.g., naive temporal comparisons across sampling-design changes; fine-scale modeling on obfuscated records).

responses.question: Is there a mechanism to report issues/errors?
responses.evidence: No issue-reporting mechanism (issue tracker, contact email) is present in the product metadata.
responses.recommendation: Provide a direct issue-reporting channel (support email or issue-tracker URL) in the metadata.

responses.question: Is the dataset available for direct download?
responses.evidence: The product is available for download through the NEON data portal.

responses.question: Is the dataset accessible via an API?
responses.evidence: Metadata and data are accessible via the NEON REST API (https://data.neonscience.org/api/v0/products/DP1.10022.001).

responses.question: Is the API type documented?
responses.evidence: The NEON API is RESTful, returning JSON.

responses.question: Is API reference/documentation available?
responses.evidence: NEON publishes API documentation for its REST endpoints, covering products, sites, and data endpoints.

responses.question: Is the API rate limit documented?
responses.evidence: NEON documents API rate limits in its general API documentation, but the limit is not stated in this product record.
responses.recommendation: Reference the applicable API rate limit (and token-based increase) from the product record for programmatic users.

responses.question: Is cloud access documented?
responses.evidence: Cloud-hosted access is not documented in the product metadata.
responses.recommendation: Document whether data are mirrored to a cloud platform (e.g., cloud-optimized formats) to support large-scale workflows.

responses.question: Is the data provided in a machine-readable format?
responses.evidence: Data/metadata are machine-readable: JSON via API and tabular data tables.

responses.question: Is the data provided in an open (non-proprietary) format?
responses.evidence: Formats are non-proprietary (JSON, and CSV data tables per NEON convention; DarwinCore archives for specimens).

responses.question: Is the data available in multiple formats?
responses.evidence: Basic and expanded data packages are offered, plus DarwinCore archives for biorepository specimens.

responses.question: Is a license documented?
responses.evidence: Data are released under NEON's data policy/citation terms and carry per-release DOIs (e.g., 10.48443/q9ne-6b77).

responses.question: Is the license standardized / machine-readable?
responses.evidence: License terms are provided as a NEON data-policy URL; no SPDX identifier is supplied.
responses.recommendation: Adopt an SPDX identifier (e.g., CC-BY-4.0) so the license is machine-readable for AI/ML registries (Hugging Face, Croissant).

responses.question: Is the presence/handling of sensitive information documented?
responses.evidence: Sensitive-species handling is documented: taxonomic IDs of species of concern are 'fuzzed', with state/federal obfuscation described in the change logs.

responses.question: Are access restrictions documented?
responses.evidence: Obfuscation of sensitive taxa and some site-level restrictions are described, but the full criteria and affected records are not enumerated.
responses.recommendation: List which taxa/sites are subject to obfuscation and the criteria used, so users can anticipate degraded location data.

responses.question: Is a secure/conditional access procedure documented?
responses.evidence: The data are openly and freely accessible with no authentication; there is no conditional/secured access gateway (sensitive taxa are obfuscated in place rather than access-gated).

responses.evidence: Scoped to CARE-governed / Indigenous/community data; not applicable to this dataset.

responses.evidence: The item captures CARE-specific provenance (actors/operations/preferences leading to a data point) for governed data; this dataset is not CARE-governed.

strengths: Persistent per-release DOIs and a stable landing page
Comprehensive abstract, methods, and sampling-design documentation
Extensive spatial and temporal coverage (all NEON terrestrial sites, 2013-present)
Multi-level quality control with external expert-taxonomist verification
Transparent change logs documenting sampling-design changes and data-quality issues
Machine-readable access via a RESTful API; open, non-proprietary formats
Documented handling of sensitive-species obfuscation and missing-data flagging
gaps: No individual creator/curator/contact names or ORCIDs
No supported-ML-task list, usage recommendations, out-of-scope guidance, or AI/ML usage history
No file checksums; explicit file-format declarations not in the retrieved metadata
License not expressed as an SPDX identifier
Bias documented only implicitly; no explicit bias/risk section
summary.overall_assessment: NEON Ground Beetles (DP1.10022.001) is strongly FAIR-compliant: persistent DOIs, rich standardized metadata, API access, open formats, and thorough methods/QC documentation. The main shortfalls are AI-readiness affordances (no ML-task or usage guidance, no AI/ML usage history, implicit-only bias documentation) and attribution/contact details (individual names, ORCIDs, funding, issue reporting). The N/A rule fired as designed on derived-dataset, text/NLP, experimental, ML-split, and CARE-governance items that do not apply to this primary observational dataset.
